hook: Michael I. Jordan earned a master's degree in mathematics from Arizona State University and a PhD in cognitive science from the University of California, San Diego in 1985. He joined the faculty of MIT in 1988, before moving to the University of California, Berkeley in 1998. At Berkeley he holds the Pehong Chen Distinguished Professorship jointly in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences and the Department of Statistics. His research connects statistics, optimization and computer science, with major contributions to probabilistic graphical models, variational inference and Bayesian nonparametric methods that shaped how modern machine learning systems reason under uncertainty. He has also been an outspoken voice pushing back on hype around artificial general intelligence, arguing in his widely read 2018 essay that the field needs a genuine engineering discipline built around real world human centered systems rather than science fiction narratives about human imitative AI.
